Claim: hotcrm epic PM `session_01DuzfS5chho38Yx1jxx9DEj` → dev branch `claude/issue-8820-dashboard-refresh-interval-seconds`

Dispatched on the maintainer's instruction, 2026-09-09, verbatim: 「继续处理所有相关任务」. The assignee and this claim are the PM's act; the dev inherits both, checks that the newest `Claim:` names its branch, and ⛔ posts no second claim and ⛔ never writes the assignee.

## ⚠️ The gap this card describes is now OPEN, not hypothetical

When this card was filed the hotcrm rename was still pending. It has since **merged** — hotcrm `main` is `965933b` (PR objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1814), and all five hotcrm dashboards now author `refreshIntervalSeconds`.

⇒ **As of now, objectui's two dashboard timers read a key that is no longer authored, so auto-refresh does not start.** The card's measured state (`refreshIntervalSeconds` = 0 occurrences on objectui `main`) was re-verified at `dcbf0b2b`; re-measure on your own base, ⛔ do not trust either SHA — objectui `main` moved once already between two readings an hour apart.

⛔ This is a **source** gate, not a release gate — maintainer: 「objectstack console 使用的是objectui源码打包，没有依赖发版本」. ⛔ Never wait on, or ask for, an objectui release.

## ⛔⛔ The trap, restated because a repo-wide replace is the obvious wrong move

**`refreshInterval` was NOT globally retired — only `dashboard.refreshInterval`.** `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` still carries 11 `refreshInterval` occurrences beside 13 `refreshIntervalSeconds`. `packages/plugin-report/src/ReportViewer.tsx:230` reads **`report.refreshInterval`**, a different schema that did **not** rename.

⇒ **Rename by carrier, never by string.** Before touching any occurrence, confirm which schema it reads from. ⛔ `packages/plugin-report/**` is out of scope and must be unchanged.

⭐ Same shape as the two-carrier trap this programme already hit once (`ViewTabSchema`: `UserFiltersSchema.tabs` live, `ListViewSchema.tabs` dead) — which is why it is called out twice.

## Re-scoped, and the record of why — from the epic PM who filed this card

**This card was a duplicate, and it was premise-false. Both were my error, and #7783 predicted the second one in writing four days before I filed.**

**Duplicate.** #7783 — *"dashboard `refreshInterval` → `refreshIntervalSeconds`: two declarations and six reader sites to move when the spec rename ships"* — was filed **2026-09-05T18:06Z**, four days before this card (2026-09-09T11:47Z). It was claimed by `os-bill` at **11:49:34Z**, two minutes *after* I filed #8820 and two hours *before* I claimed it, and folded into the #8772 family. Its implementation is open draft PR **#8783**, green and clean, `Fixes #7783`. **Six of the eight files the dev on this card touched are in that diff.** I filed into this repo without searching its own backlog first.

**Premise-false.** #7783 states the unblock condition verbatim: *"⛔ Do not start this before the rename is installable here. The unblock condition is **not** 'the upstream PR merged' — it is `@objectstack/spec` published with `refreshIntervalSeconds`, **and this repo's dependency moved onto it**. A card dispatched before the consumer can install the new key comes back premise-false, because the schema it must match does not exist in the installed package yet."*

That is exactly what happened. This repo's lockfile resolves a spec **below 17.4.0**, whose strict `DashboardSchema` **refuses `refreshIntervalSeconds` by name** — `safeParse` gives `unrecognized_keys`. The dev measured it; I re-derived the lockfile leg independently. So this card's asks 2 and 3 (the published `inputs` row, the config-panel key, the i18n key) **could not be done at all** without the dependency bump — which is PR #8783. Two triage seats had already measured both legs FALSE on #7783, and filing #8820 discarded that analysis.

⇒ **The rename is deleted from this card's scope.** It belongs to #7783 and lands in #8783. ⛔ Nothing here reassigns, reopens or touches either — this is a record, not a request.

## What survives, and why the card is not simply closed

Two asks were genuinely **absent** from #8783, and they are this repo's own quality question rather than the rename's:

1. **A test that observes the interval firing.** #8783's dashboard test edits are all **declaration pins** to a schema — they stay green if the timer never fires. That is the class this epic exists to retire.
2. **The timer exists twice, byte-identical**, in `DashboardGridLayout` and `DashboardRenderer`.

The dev built both anyway, on branch `claude/issue-8820-dashboard-refresh-interval-seconds` at **`e5d95e1a`** (pushed, ⛔ **no PR** — it would have fought #8783 for six files): one `useDashboardAutoRefresh` hook, and a 16-case pin mounting both components and asserting `onRefresh` **call counts** under fake timers, ablation-proven (6 of 16 go red when the key is removed from the reader; restore verified by blob hash). The card body above is now exactly those two pieces, `Blocked-by` #8783, with the instruction to drop the pre-bump both-spelling shim on rebase since the old key becomes a parse-refusing tombstone.

## Two corrections the dev measured that belong on the record

- **`refreshInterval` has 39 occurrences on `e9d92120`, not the 26 this card claimed.** The per-carrier breakdown is in the body. ⭐ `types/src/data.ts:1378` is **milliseconds** — a name-based sweep would have corrupted it.
- ⚠️ **#7783's table has one stale row.** It says `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts:740` carries objectui's own re-declaration of `refreshInterval` on `DashboardComponentSchema`. On `e9d92120` that is no longer true — `DashboardComponentSchema` derives its spec fields **by reference** via `SpecDashboardFields` (objectstack#4115), so it picks the renamed key up automatically on the bump. The local declaration that remains, at `complex.zod.ts:1154`, belongs to **`DashboardConfigSchema`** — a different carrier. #8783 appears to have handled this correctly; flagged so nobody re-reads the stale row and "fixes" something that is already right.

## The process fix, adopted

The cross-repo filing path now searches the **consumer repo's own backlog** before filing, not only the originating repo's. This card is the reason.
